title: a-pane-declares-its-view
intention: A PANE DECLARES ITS VIEW AND ITS BOUNDS; THE SURFACE DISPATCHES. Two joined moves on the presentation surface: (1) grow render_pane's kind dispatch from {chat, everything-else-as-<pre>} into a small CLOSED vocabulary of view primitives (record / table / sequence / tree / scalar / chat), one pure `data -> html` function each, with <pre> demoted from default to explicit FALLBACK; (2) let a pane be BOUNDED — a device answers a request-carried cursor with `{cursor, window, count}`, so a log or a history can be read a piece at a time and can say WHICH piece it is showing. The bound must reach the source (a file seek, a SQL LIMIT); slicing a fully-materialised list in Python is cosmetic and buys nothing.
why:
The <pre> was CORRECT when it was written — render_pane's own docstring says 'honest and complete for introspection', which is exactly right when you do not yet know the shapes. Akien's ruling 2026-07-29: 'we needed that level of simplicity when we wrote it, but we don't need that level of simplicity now.' It is outgrown, not wrong. Two things came due together: rich views (pretty JSON in a monospace block is not a face Telos 2 can rest on) and the fact that some panes — logs above all — carry MORE THAN WE SHOULD TRY TO FIT INTO MEMORY AS A UNIT (Akien, same conversation). MEASURED: there is no bound anywhere in the chain today. BaseShim.active_page() takes NO ARGUMENTS and assembles the whole page (shim.py:168); a pane is {kind, label, data} with no cursor, no total, no more-flag (shim.py:190); render_pane dumps pane['data'] into one <pre> (render.py:182). A 1,200-row log would be built in full, held in memory, and rendered entire.

THIS IS GROWTH ALONG AN EXISTING GRAIN, NOT A REWRITE — and that is the whole reason it is cheap. render_pane ALREADY dispatches on kind (chat is the proven first instance) and already emits data-kind on the section, which is the hook a stylesheet needs. And the bounded-read contract is ALREADY SETTLED IN-HOUSE: charter/projector.py's project() returns exactly {cursor, window, count}, with 'count = the full length, so the window's boundedness stays visible' — which is, verbatim, the Law 7 requirement a scrollable diagnostic pane needs. _window() even dispatches on a RULE DICT ({kind: count, n} / {kind: since_gate}, ValueError on unknown), the same declarative shape. So the surface reuses the projector's contract rather than inventing a second vocabulary for the same idea.
traces_to: Telos 2 — Cairn has a USER; a face made of pretty-printed JSON is a placeholder, and the librarian's interface rests on this surface

Law 7, both halves — a presentation surface may collapse an error into a coherent shape, so the FALLBACK stays (an unclassified pane must render completely rather than be dropped by a renderer that does not recognise it); and a windowed diagnostic view must SAY 'rows 40-60 of 1204', because a window that does not announce its bounds is a silent truncation

Law 6 — the cursor rides the REQUEST, never the server: web_server's falsifier (3) already reds if the surface accretes its own state or cache of device internals, and a scroll position is device internals. The falsifier did the design work
Law 4 — escaping and the data/render split stay physics; the device declares a KIND (data), never markup
Law 1 — one renderer per kind written once, and the projector's {cursor, window, count} contract reused rather than re-derived
[[shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll]] — a bounded read is cheaper per view, and a page move is a REQUEST (an event), never a timer

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate: teeth beside the code (cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/), under the tester with the netns seal — and the whole point of the shape is that it STAYS PROVABLE WITHOUT A SOCKET OR A BROWSER, as the existing proofs are. Each view kind is a pure total `data -> html` function with its own tooth; an unknown kind falls through to the <pre> fallback and renders COMPLETELY (a tooth asserts this, because a rich renderer silently eating unclassified data is the failure mode); every device string still escaped (the existing injection tooth must green unchanged); a bounded pane reports {cursor, window, count} and the rendered page STATES its bounds; prev/next are ordinary anchors carrying the cursor, so the pager is exercised by the proof with no browser. Live gate: one real device's log or history read a piece at a time through a running listener, and the SAME address served as JSON as well as HTML.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) the renderer SNIFFS the data to guess a kind — kinds are DECLARED by the device that owns the data; sniffing is render logic inferring device semantics, which is the wrong-shape signal web_server's falsifier already names; (2) the <pre> fallback is deleted rather than demoted, so an unclassified pane renders partially or not at all; (3) a cursor, scroll position, or page cache appears in the web server (falsifier 3 of its charter — the surface owns no device state); (4) COSMETIC WINDOWING: a bounded pane's handler materialises the whole sequence and slices it in Python — the bound must reach the source, or the memory was still spent and nothing was bought; (5) a rendered window does not state which piece of how many it is showing; (6) ANY auto-refresh, tail-follow timer, or scroll-triggered auto-load appears — the next request is the event, and this is the single likeliest site in the whole system for a poller to sneak back in ([[reaching-for-daemons-is-drift]]: backstop / just-in-case is where they reappear, and tailing FEELS like it needs a clock); (7) HTML is authored in a shim instead of DATA (the data/render split has failed and the tester can no longer probe the same protocol the UI renders).
falsifier.horizon: re-read when: a second consumer needs a view kind not in the closed set (the set is deliberately small and the FIRST addition tells us whether the vocabulary was chosen well, or whether kinds should carry a schema instead); the diagnostic slice lands and gives the sequence kind its first real load ([[diagnostic-logging-method]] — the log-processor's on-demand slice IS this pane's data provider, so the two are halves of one thing); htmx or any client library is genuinely wanted (see the graft note in dependencies); a device's history outgrows the projector's materialise-then-slice, which is the moment bound-reaches-the-source stops being optional there too.

how: Grow render_pane's kind dispatch from if/elif to a declared view-spec per pane. A pane declares its view (text, table, chart) and bounds (refresh, scroll); the surface reads the spec and dispatches.

chart_notes.constrain: WHAT IS THE CLOSED SET, and who may add to it? A small fixed vocabulary is the whole value (Grafana's lesson); an open set drifts back to one bespoke view per device, which is what the <pre> was avoiding in the first place. Candidate: record / table / sequence / tree / scalar / chat + the absent and fallback shapes that already exist. Settle also: does a kind carry a SCHEMA (rjsf's answer) or is the kind name enough (Grafana's answer)? Kind-name-only is the cheaper honest start and the horizon says the first new kind will tell us
chart_notes.survey: which of today's real panes fall into which kind (the honest census — if most collapse to `record` then the vocabulary is smaller than proposed); how the librarian's chat pane got its rich view, since it is the proven precedent and the second instance should mirror its shape not invent one; what the LOGGING pane was going to be (web_server filed edge — 'the LOGGING pane reads real emission' is still open) and whether the diagnostic slice is its provider; whether ANY existing device has a sequence long enough to make bound-reaches-the-source bite TODAY, because if none does, that half is a hypothesis-driven build and should be scoped or deferred accordingly
chart_notes.decompose: the two halves (view vocabulary / bounded reads) are ONE ticket by intention but may not share a proof story: the vocabulary is pure-function teeth in render.py, while bounded reads change active_page's signature and reach into shim + server. If they do not share a proof story, that is the finding that earns a split — check it, do not assume it (the rule nothing-rides-loose's decompose note states)
chart_notes.triage: the vocabulary is the half with a user-visible win and no signature change — it goes first. Bounded reads change active_page's contract, which every device's shim rides, so it wants its own careful pass. NOTE: neither half blocks a-node-holds-one-claim, and a-node-holds-one-claim blocks the stone queue — this one waits its turn behind THE thing
chart_notes.hypothesize: label as hypotheses: (i) that a closed set of six kinds covers substantially all real panes (survey's census either supports this or shrinks it); (ii) that plain hypermedia anchors are ergonomically sufficient without htmx — the honest falsifier being a real human finding them tedious, which is a measurement, not an opinion; (iii) that bound-reaches-the-source is needed TODAY rather than at the first big log
chart_notes.validate: the instrument, run twice, plus a live fire per half: a real device page rendering rich views through the listener, and one real sequence read a piece at a time with its bounds stated on the page — and the same address served as JSON, proving the one-protocol claim
